assumptions: Equation (5.2)'s componentwise base residual bound holds.
The correction magnitude satisfies the Neumann inequality derived before equation (5.4).
Under equation (5.6), M₁ is an entrywise nonnegative inverse action for I-P.

conditions.N: The fixed statement and P03 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p03_t3_componentwise_residual_recurrence {n : ℕ} (us u gammaR : ℝ) (M1 P : Fin n → Fin n → ℝ) ... : ∀ i, |newResidual i| ≤ us * |oldResidual i| + (1+us) * (M1 |oldResidual|)_i + ...
formal_statement.plain_language: A nonnegative M-matrix inverse resolves the correction inequality and yields Theorem 5.1's componentwise residual recurrence.

informal_proof: Subtract the P-action from the correction inequality, premultiply by the nonnegative inverse M₁, use its inverse-action identity, distribute M₁ over the old residual and data terms, and substitute the result into equation (5.2).
informal_statement: The exact Wᵢ and yᵢ componentwise recurrence of Theorem 5.1 with the matrix products packaged as P and M₁.
